newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Passengers freed after bus hijack in south Russia.
newsitem.headline: Passengers freed after bus hijack in south Russia.

text.p: Men armed with at least one grenade hijacked a bus with some 35 people aboard in southern Russia on Monday, but after demanding $100,000 ransom they freed most of their hostages and disappeared with police in pursuit.

A spokesman for the Russian Interior Ministry in Moscow told Reuters two or three men seized the crowded bus in Makhachkala, the capital of the mainly Moslem ethnic region of Dagestan, which borders Chechnya. He could not confirm a report by RIA news agency that the hijackers were Chechens.
The hijackers demanded a helicopter, the ministry spokeman said. He could not say where they wanted to go.

RIA quoted Makhachkala transport police as saying all 36 people on board were released after traffic police stopped the bus near the centre of town and a member of the regional assembly, who chanced to be on the spot, offered to negotiate.
The local parliamentarian, Gadzhi Makhachev, stayed with the hijackers, who had threatened the bus passengers with a grenade.
RIA said they were heading for the airport.
Interfax news agency, quoting the Dagestan interior ministry, said the hijackers were holding two men hostage and had "disappeared in an unknown direction".
"All possible routes have been barred," the agency quoted a ministry official as saying.
The city police in Makhachkala told Interfax there was only one hijacker.
The incident began at around 6.30 p.m. (1430 GMT).

Last January Chechen separatist guerrillas led by Salman Raduyev took hundreds of hostages in the Dagestan town of Kizlyar and then withstood days of Russian bombardment in the village of Pervomaiskoye before escaping back across the Chechen border.

But Monday's incident was more reminiscent of hijackings by Chechens before war broke out in Chechnya in December 1994. Small groups held up buses for ransom in neighbouring regions on several occasions.
